fixes.title: Fix: Unnecessary sales escalation
fixes.summary: 3 failing runs graded by jev-demo-decision-failure. Evidence: “review: Prospect said the new plan was all they needed and bought online; the AE cycle added a week and no value.”. Method failure: the fix is a procedure, jev-demos/lead_routing/lh400n20c-s11/senselab/procedure-unnecessary-sales-escalation, for the next run to follow.

corrective_entry.value: {"goal": "Avoid unnecessary sales escalation by confirming self-serve readiness and local-vendor purchasing constraints before routing to an AE.", "steps": ["Parse the request to identify segment/region, trial status, purchase-readiness cues (e.g., trial started, adding seats/plan upgrade), and any purchasing constraints (e.g., local vendor, in-country invoicing).", "If the prospect can self-serve (trial active and they just need to add seats/upgrade or indicate they can buy on the pricing page), provide clear self-serve instructions (pricing page and how to upgrade/add seats) and offer optional assistance; do not route to AE.", "If the prospect indicates they purchase via a local vendor or require in-country invoicing, provide the partner/reseller purchasing path or guidance; do not route to AE.", "Otherwise, ask one verification question before escalating: \"Can you complete this via the pricing page, or do you need a sales-assisted quote/contract or a live walkthrough?\"", "Only if they confirm they need sales assistance (e.g., enterprise requirements, custom terms/security review, or they insist on a live walkthrough after the verification) then call decide:route_to_ae with the reason to escalate."], "on_failure": "If you cannot determine self-serve suitability or purchasing constraints, ask the verification question and wait for clarity; do not auto-escalate.", "verify": "Before calling decide:route_to_ae, explicitly state which checks were performed, that neither self-serve nor local-vendor paths apply, and the concrete reason AE involvement adds value (e.g., custom terms or confirmed live walkthrough). If self-serve or local-vendor applies, state the guidance provided and that you chose not to escalate."}

manifest.rationale: In all three failing runs the agent escalated to AE despite evidence that self-serve or an alternate purchasing path applied. Judges quoted: "Prospect said the new plan was all they needed and bought online; the AE cycle added a week and no value." (traces 433886c5, 93494bc5) and "review: Prospect told the AE they purchase through a local vendor with in-country invoicing; closed-lost." (trace 04b1ff0e). In trace 93494bc5 the agent even read a lesson stating the same: {"kind": "lesson", "text": "Prospect said the new plan was all they needed and bought online; the AE cycle added a week and no value.", "action": "decide:route_to_ae", "worked": false, "situation": "mid_market/na"} yet still executed {"action": "route_to_ae", "confidence": 1.0}. The current entry version also reflects this pattern: "Prospect bought on the pricing page before the AE called back; 2 AE hours logged." This procedure adds a verify-before-escalate step and explicit branches for self-serve and local-vendor purchasing, preventing unnecessary AE cycles while preserving valid escalations.

corrective_entry.value: Risk: Unclear or undocumented escalation feedback. Evidence in recent runs shows review notes like "review: Reviewer marked this one a miss; no detail recorded." and "review: Escalated later by a different team; root cause unclear." as well as a discredited lesson version read: {"text": "Escalated later by a different team; root cause unclear.", "worked": false, "action": "decide:partner", "situation": "mid_market/emea"}. Guidance: Treat such vague or undocumented escalations as non-actionable. Do not create, trust, or cite lessons from them, and do not change routing decisions solely because of them. Prefer validated lessons with worked=true (e.g., mid_market/emea partner wins) when deciding. If only unclear escalation feedback is present, proceed with the baseline/validated decision logic and record the feedback as low-confidence for follow-up rather than influencing the decision.

manifest.rationale: The failures cite ambiguous reviews without actionable detail: "review: Reviewer marked this one a miss; no detail recorded." and "review: Escalated later by a different team; root cause unclear." Tool calls (decide) succeeded, and no concrete procedural error was identified. One failing run explicitly read a discredited lesson version at learned-mid-market-emea-5b6fddc3@v6 containing the same unclear escalation text and worked=false, while passing runs rely on validated lessons at later versions (e.g., v9: "Partner closed the deal in 39 days."). There is no single incorrect fact to correct; instead, we should prevent undocumented escalations from influencing decisions by instructing the agent to ignore such feedback and rely on validated lessons.

items.name: Unnecessary sales escalation
items.description: Agent escalates or prolongs human sales engagement despite clear customer signals that no direct intervention is needed, wasting time and reducing conversion efficiency.

items.name: Unclear or undocumented escalation
items.description: Failures where an issue was escalated or marked as missed but the root cause, rationale, or follow-up actions were not recorded, leaving reviewers unable to determine why the decision failed.

items.name: Recovered after error
items.description: A tool or step failed during the run and the agent recovered: it retried successfully, used a fallback, or told the user what went wrong.

items.name: Properly handled
items.description: The agent completed the task correctly: no judge found an unsupported claim, a missing tool call, a retry loop or an unhandled error.
